title: PBC implies injective acyclicity
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ holds for torsion abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-property], then $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ holds for every prime $r$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property]. Explicitly, after any cartesian base change [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], the higher direct images $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I$ vanish for $q>0$ for every injective sheaf $I$ of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives), proof of (1) => (2); source Lean docstring BaseChangeProperty.lean lines 198-205

proof.text: Fix a prime $r$, a morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, a cartesian square with maps $f'$ and $g'$, and an injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf $I$ on $X_{\Et}$. Its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion (it is killed by $r$), so the PBC hypothesis applies to the complex concentrated in degree $0$ with value $I$. The resulting specified derived exchange morphism is an isomorphism $g^{-1}Rf_*I\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}I$. In Lean, use the finite coefficient ring to obtain IsTorsionModuleSheaf, its comparison with local torsion, and the torsion-sheaf characterizations to obtain the canonical filtered-colimit torsion predicate of PBC.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2), first sentence: apply the base-change hypothesis to the injective sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: Use the constant-ring module-sheaf equivalence to send the module-valued sheaf I to a SheafOfModules object J. The equivalence preserves injectivity and supplies a natural isomorphism between the underlying abelian sheaves. Apply the module-injective direct-image acyclicity lemma to f and J in each positive natural degree. Map the underlying-sheaf isomorphism through the single, right-derived direct-image and cohomology functors to obtain vanishing for I. A positive integer degree is a positive natural degree, so this covers all q > 0. Only positive-degree vanishing is needed; no degree-zero identification is used.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2): the source has no homology outside degree zero because the injective sheaf is acyclic

proof.text: The inverse-image functor g^{-1} on abelian etale sheaves is exact, as provided by its existing finite-limit, finite-colimit and additive instances. Its bounded-below derived functor commutes with cohomology via Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso. Apply g^{-1} to the zero cohomology object from Step 2 and transport through this comparison isomorphism. Thus H^q(g^{-1}Rf_*I) is zero for q > 0.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2): exact inverse image preserves the concentration in degree zero

proof.text: Apply the cohomology functor H^q to the exchange isomorphism from Step 1. Transfer zero-ness from the source in Step 3 to its target. Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor identifies derived inverse image of I[0] with the pullback abelian sheaf in degree zero. Map this isomorphism through the right-derived direct image and then cohomology. The resulting zero object is precisely R^q f'_* g'^{-1} I required in the injective-acyclicity property.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2): transfer the vanishing across the base-change isomorphism

proof.text: The square, the prime $r$, and the injective $I$ were arbitrary. Therefore the vanishing in Step 4 is precisely $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ for this prime, and varying $r$ gives $\mathrm{IA}(f)$ as required.

split_report.summary: Split the PBC-to-IA direction into five steps: specialize PBC to an injective prime-field module sheaf in degree zero, use module-injective direct-image acyclicity and the degree-zero derived identification, transport vanishing through exact inverse image and cohomology, transfer it across the exchange isomorphism, and conclude the quantified IA property. The source's sorry-free theorem is module-valued for arbitrary coefficients and was checked but retained as a related declaration rather than an exact attachment.
